standard_text: Addition and subtraction of decimals to hundredths

key_big: Line up the decimal points, then add or subtract like whole numbers.
key_sub: Tenths go with tenths and hundredths with hundredths. 10 tenths make 1 whole, so 0.6 + 0.5 = 1.1, not 0.11. Estimate to check: 4.5 + 2.37 is about 7, so the answer is 6.87.
body_html:
The idea: add tenths to tenths, hundredths to hundredths

A decimal is made of ones, tenths and hundredths. You can only add or subtract parts of the same size. So add tenths to tenths and hundredths to hundredths, just like ones to ones.

Line up the decimal points

In columns, put point under point. Then ones are under ones, tenths under tenths and hundredths under hundredths. If one number has fewer places, write a zero: 4.5 = 4.50. A zero at the end does not change the value.

Regroup like whole numbers

10 hundredths make 1 tenth, and 10 tenths make 1 one. When a column makes 10 or more, regroup. The 1 can cross the decimal point.

To take a decimal from a whole number, write the whole number with a point and zeros: 10 = 10.00.

Estimate first, then check

Round each number to the nearest whole number. 4.5 + 2.37 is about 5 + 2 = 7, so 6.87 makes sense and 2.82 does not. Check a subtraction by adding back: 6.54 + 3.46 = 10.

Money in Canada: cash and card

Canada has no pennies. When you pay with cash, the total is rounded to the nearest 5¢. When you pay by debit or credit card, you pay the exact amount.

Total ends inCash totalExample
1¢ or 2¢Round down to 0¢$7.42 → $7.40
3¢ or 4¢Round up to 5¢$7.43 → $7.45
6¢ or 7¢Round down to 5¢$7.47 → $7.45
8¢ or 9¢Round up to the next 10¢$7.48 → $7.50
Example

A muffin costs $1.89 and milk costs $1.48. How much do you pay with cash? With a card?

Add: $1.89 + $1.48 = $3.37. Card: the exact amount, $3.37. Cash: $3.37 is closer to $3.35 than to $3.40.

Answer: cash $3.35, card $3.37

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Lining up the last digits (4.5 + 2.37 = 2.82)Line up the decimal points. Write 4.5 as 4.50
Dropping the decimal point (4.5 + 2.37 = 687)Bring the point straight down into the answer
Writing 11 tenths as 0.11 (0.6 + 0.5 = 0.11)10 tenths make 1 one: 0.6 + 0.5 = 1.1
Not writing the zeros (10 − 3.46 = 7.46)Write 10 as 10.00, then regroup to subtract

faq.q: How do you add and subtract decimals in Grade 4?
faq.a: Line up the decimal points, write zeros in empty places, then add or subtract from the right like whole numbers: 4.5 + 2.37 = 4.50 + 2.37 = 6.87.
0.6 + 0.5 is 6 tenths + 5 tenths = 11 tenths, and 10 tenths make 1 whole, so the answer is 1.1. 0.11 is only 11 hundredths, which is less than 0.6.

faq.q: How is cash rounded in Canada without pennies?
faq.a: A cash total is rounded to the nearest 5¢: totals ending in 1, 2, 6 or 7 cents round down, and totals ending in 3, 4, 8 or 9 cents round up. Debit and credit card payments are charged the exact amount.

faq.q: Is adding and subtracting decimals on the Grade 4 FSA?
faq.a: It can be. The Grade 4 FSA numeracy section is based on the BC curriculum, and adding and subtracting decimals to hundredths is a Grade 4 learning standard, often met in money and measurement problems.

sets.title: Add and subtract tenths with models

items.q: The bar is 1 whole cut into 10 equal parts. The green part is 0.3 and the yellow part is 0.4. What is 0.3 + 0.4?
items.e: Each part is 1 tenth, or 0.1. 0.3 is 3 tenths and 0.4 is 4 tenths. Together: 3 + 4 = 7 tenths = 0.7.

items.q: The bar is 1 whole cut into 10 equal parts. The green part is 0.2 and the yellow part is 0.5. What is 0.2 + 0.5?
items.e: Each part is 1 tenth, or 0.1. 0.2 is 2 tenths and 0.5 is 5 tenths. Together: 2 + 5 = 7 tenths = 0.7.

items.q: The bar is 1 whole cut into 10 equal parts. The green part is 0.6 and the yellow part is 0.3. What is 0.6 + 0.3?
items.e: Each part is 1 tenth, or 0.1. 0.6 is 6 tenths and 0.3 is 3 tenths. Together: 6 + 3 = 9 tenths = 0.9.

items.q: The bar is 1 whole cut into 10 equal parts. The green part is 0.1 and the yellow part is 0.7. What is 0.1 + 0.7?
items.e: Each part is 1 tenth, or 0.1. 0.1 is 1 tenth and 0.7 is 7 tenths. Together: 1 + 7 = 8 tenths = 0.8.

items.q: The bar is 1 whole cut into 10 equal parts. The green part is 0.4 and the yellow part is 0.4. What is 0.4 + 0.4?
items.e: Each part is 1 tenth, or 0.1. 0.4 is 4 tenths and 0.4 is 4 tenths. Together: 4 + 4 = 8 tenths = 0.8.

items.q: Each bar is 1 whole. The green part is 0.6 and the yellow part is 0.5. What is 0.6 + 0.5?
items.e: 6 tenths + 5 tenths = 6 + 5 = 11 tenths. 10 tenths fill one whole bar, so the sum is 1 whole and 1 tenth = 1.1. It is not 0.11: the sum is more than 1 whole, and 0.11 is less than 1.

items.q: Each bar is 1 whole. The green part is 0.8 and the yellow part is 0.7. What is 0.8 + 0.7?
items.e: 8 tenths + 7 tenths = 8 + 7 = 15 tenths. 10 tenths fill one whole bar, so the sum is 1 whole and 5 tenths = 1.5. It is not 0.15: the sum is more than 1 whole, and 0.15 is less than 1.

items.q: Each bar is 1 whole. The green part is 0.9 and the yellow part is 0.4. What is 0.9 + 0.4?
items.e: 9 tenths + 4 tenths = 9 + 4 = 13 tenths. 10 tenths fill one whole bar, so the sum is 1 whole and 3 tenths = 1.3. It is not 0.13: the sum is more than 1 whole, and 0.13 is less than 1.

items.q: Each bar is 1 whole. The green part is 0.7 and the yellow part is 0.6. What is 0.7 + 0.6?
items.e: 7 tenths + 6 tenths = 7 + 6 = 13 tenths. 10 tenths fill one whole bar, so the sum is 1 whole and 3 tenths = 1.3. It is not 0.13: the sum is more than 1 whole, and 0.13 is less than 1.

items.q: The bar is 1 whole. 0.8 is shaded. The parts with an X are taken away. What is 0.8 − 0.3?
items.e: 0.8 is 8 tenths. Take away 0.3 (3 tenths). The parts without an X are left: 8 − 3 = 5 tenths. 0.8 − 0.3 = 0.5.

items.q: The bar is 1 whole. 0.9 is shaded. The parts with an X are taken away. What is 0.9 − 0.4?
items.e: 0.9 is 9 tenths. Take away 0.4 (4 tenths). The parts without an X are left: 9 − 4 = 5 tenths. 0.9 − 0.4 = 0.5.

items.q: Each bar is 1 whole. 1.2 is shaded. The parts with an X are taken away. What is 1.2 − 0.5?
items.e: 1.2 is 12 tenths. Take away 0.5 (5 tenths). The parts without an X are left: 12 − 5 = 7 tenths. 1.2 − 0.5 = 0.7. (Do not take the smaller digit from the bigger one: 1.2 − 0.5 is not 1.3.)

items.q: Each bar is 1 whole. 1.4 is shaded. The parts with an X are taken away. What is 1.4 − 0.6?
items.e: 1.4 is 14 tenths. Take away 0.6 (6 tenths). The parts without an X are left: 14 − 6 = 8 tenths. 1.4 − 0.6 = 0.8. (Do not take the smaller digit from the bigger one: 1.4 − 0.6 is not 1.2.)

items.q: Start at 0.8 and jump 0.5 to the right. Where do you land? What is 0.8 + 0.5?
items.e: Count on 5 tenths from 0.8: 0.9, 1, 1.1, 1.2, 1.3. A jump of 0.2 gets to 1, then 0.3 more gets to 1.3. (1.2 counts 0.8 as the first jump. 0.13 forgets that 10 tenths make 1.)

items.q: Start at 1.5 and jump 0.7 to the left. Where do you land? What is 1.5 − 0.7?
items.e: Jump back 0.5 from 1.5 to get to 1. Then jump back 0.2 more: 1 − 0.2 = 0.8. Check: 0.8 + 0.7 = 1.5. (1.2 takes 5 from 7 instead of 7 from 15 tenths.)

items.q: Emma says 0.6 + 0.5 = 0.11. What is the correct answer?
items.e: 6 tenths + 5 tenths = 11 tenths. 10 tenths make 1 whole, so 11 tenths = 1 whole and 1 tenth = 1.1. 0.11 is only 11 hundredths, which is less than 0.6 alone.

items.q: How many tenths are in 1.3?
items.e: 1 whole is 10 tenths. 1.3 = 10 tenths + 3 tenths = 13 tenths.

items.q: What number goes in the box? 0.4 + ☐ = 1
items.e: 1 whole is 10 tenths and 0.4 is 4 tenths. 10 − 4 = 6 tenths = 0.6. Check: 0.4 + 0.6 = 1.

items.q: What is 2.4 + 1.3?
items.e: Add ones to ones and tenths to tenths. Ones: 2 + 1 = 3. Tenths: 4 + 3 = 7 tenths. Answer: 3.7. Keep the decimal point: 37 drops it.

items.q: What is 3.5 − 1.8?
items.e: Tenths: 5 − 8 needs a regroup. 1 one becomes 10 tenths: 15 − 8 = 7. Ones: 2 − 1 = 1. Answer: 1.7. Check: 1.7 + 1.8 = 3.5. (2.3 takes 5 from 8 instead of regrouping.)

items.q: You add 3.42 + 5.17 in columns with the decimal points lined up. Which digit of 5.17 goes under the 4?
items.e: The 4 in 3.42 is in the tenths place. Tenths go under tenths: the tenths digit of 5.17 is 1. (7 is the hundredths digit, so it goes under the 2.)

items.q: To add 2.3 + 1.45, you write 2.3 with two decimal places. Which number is equal to 2.3?
items.e: A zero at the end of a decimal does not change its value: 2.3 = 2 ones and 3 tenths = 2.30. 2.03 is wrong: it moves the 3 to the hundredths place.

items.q: Mateo lined up the last digits and got 2.77. What is the correct sum?
items.e: Line up the decimal points, not the last digits: 4.50 + 2.32. Hundredths: 0 + 2 = 2. Tenths: 5 + 3 = 8. Ones: 4 + 2 = 6. Answer: 6.82. Estimate: 5 + 2 = 7, so 2.77 is far too small.

items.q: To find 12 + 3.45, you can write 12 with a decimal point. Which number is equal to 12?
items.e: A whole number has its decimal point after the ones digit, so 12 = 12.00. Then the 2 ones sit over the 3 ones: 12.00 + 3.45 = 15.45.

items.q: Kai lined up the last digits and got 2.58. What is the correct sum?
items.e: 13 is a whole number, so its point is after the 3: 13 = 13.00 (not 0.13). Line up the points: 13.00 + 2.45. Hundredths: 0 + 5 = 5. Tenths: 0 + 4 = 4. Ones: 3 + 2 = 5. Tens: bring down 1. Answer: 15.45.

items.q: Which shows 6.4 − 2.3 with the decimal points lined up?
items.e: Write the number you start with on top and the number you take away below it. Put point under point, so ones are under ones and tenths under tenths. Then 6.4 − 2.3 = 4.1.

items.q: Add.
items.e: Line up the decimal points. Tenths: 1 + 4 = 5. Ones: 7 + 1 = 8. Answer: 8.5. Check: 8.5 − 1.4 = 7.1.

items.q: What is 9.9 − 8.8?
items.e: Line up the decimal points. Tenths: 9 − 8 = 1. Ones: 9 − 8 = 1. Answer: 1.1. Check: 1.1 + 8.8 = 9.9.

items.q: Add.

items.q: What is 9.33 − 2.1?

items.q: Add.
items.e: Line up the decimal points. Tenths: 3 + 1 = 4. Ones: 1 + 3 = 4. Tens: bring down 6. Answer: 64.4. Check: 64.4 − 63.1 = 1.3.

items.q: What is 57.7 − 4.5?

items.q: Add.
items.e: Line up the decimal points. Hundredths: 4 + 3 = 7. Tenths: 1 + 0 = 1. Ones: 3 + 6 = 9. Tens: bring down 3. Answer: 39.17. Check: 39.17 − 36.03 = 3.14.
Line up the decimal points. Hundredths: 9 − 3 = 6. Tenths: 4 − 3 = 1. Ones: 9 − 0 = 9. Tens: 9 − 6 = 3. Answer: 39.16. Check: 39.16 + 60.33 = 99.49.

items.q: Add.
items.e: Line up the decimal points. Write 50.3 as 50.30. Hundredths: 0 + 4 = 4. Tenths: 3 + 1 = 4. Ones: 0 + 9 = 9. Tens: bring down 5. Answer: 59.44. Check: 59.44 − 9.14 = 50.3.

items.q: Add.

items.q: The grid is 1 whole. The green part is 0.45 and the yellow part is 0.38. What is 0.45 + 0.38?
items.e: Each small square is 0.01 and each column is 0.1. 0.45 = 45 hundredths and 0.38 = 38 hundredths. Together: 45 + 38 = 83 hundredths = 0.83. In columns: hundredths 5 + 8 = 13, so regroup 1 tenth.

items.q: The grid is 1 whole. The green part is 0.27 and the yellow part is 0.56. What is 0.27 + 0.56?
items.e: Each small square is 0.01 and each column is 0.1. 0.27 = 27 hundredths and 0.56 = 56 hundredths. Together: 27 + 56 = 83 hundredths = 0.83. In columns: hundredths 7 + 6 = 13, so regroup 1 tenth.

items.q: Each grid is 1 whole. The green part is 0.7 and the yellow part is 0.65. What is 0.7 + 0.65?
items.e: 0.7 = 70 hundredths and 0.65 = 65 hundredths. 70 + 65 = 135 hundredths. 100 hundredths fill one whole grid, so the sum is 1 whole and 35 hundredths = 1.35. (0.72 lines up the last digits: 0.7 is 0.70, not 0.07.)

items.q: The grid is 1 whole. 0.82 is shaded. The squares with an X are taken away. What is 0.82 − 0.35?
items.e: 0.82 is 82 hundredths. Take away 35 hundredths: 82 − 35 = 47 hundredths = 0.47. In columns: 2 − 5 needs a regroup, so 1 tenth becomes 10 hundredths: 12 − 5 = 7, then 7 − 3 = 4.

items.q: 10 hundredths make 1 tenth. What is 0.08 + 0.05?
items.e: 8 hundredths + 5 hundredths = 13 hundredths = 1 tenth and 3 hundredths = 0.13. (0.03 forgets the regrouped tenth. 1.3 puts the point in the wrong place.)

items.q: Add.
items.e: Line up the decimal points. Hundredths: 9 + 7 = 16, write 6 and regroup 1 tenth. Tenths: 8 + 4 + 1 = 13, write 3 and regroup 1 one. Ones: 9 + 8 + 1 = 18, write 18. Answer: 18.36. Check: 18.36 − 8.47 = 9.89.
Line up the decimal points. Hundredths: 9 − 7 = 2. Tenths: 3 − 9 needs a regroup. 1 one becomes 10 tenths: 13 − 9 = 4. Ones: 4 − 3 = 1. Answer: 1.42. Check: 1.42 + 3.97 = 5.39.

items.q: Add.
items.e: Line up the decimal points. Write 6.5 as 6.50. Hundredths: 5 + 0 = 5. Tenths: 8 + 5 = 13, write 3 and regroup 1 one. Ones: 8 + 6 + 1 = 15, write 15. Answer: 15.35. Check: 15.35 − 6.5 = 8.85.

items.q: What is 9.04 − 4.5?
items.e: Line up the decimal points. Write 4.5 as 4.50. Hundredths: 4 − 0 = 4. Tenths: 0 − 5 needs a regroup. 1 one becomes 10 tenths: 10 − 5 = 5. Ones: 8 − 4 = 4. Answer: 4.54. Check: 4.54 + 4.5 = 9.04.

items.q: Add.
items.e: Line up the decimal points. Hundredths: 3 + 8 = 11, write 1 and regroup 1 tenth. Tenths: 9 + 7 + 1 = 17, write 7 and regroup 1 one. Ones: 4 + 4 + 1 = 9. Tens: bring down 4. Answer: 49.71. Check: 49.71 − 44.78 = 4.93.

Line up the decimal points. Hundredths: 2 − 8 needs a regroup. 1 tenth becomes 10 hundredths: 12 − 8 = 4. Tenths: 4 − 2 = 2. Ones: 7 − 9 needs a regroup. 1 ten becomes 10 ones: 17 − 9 = 8. Answer: 8.24. Check: 8.24 + 9.28 = 17.52.

items.q: Add.
items.e: Line up the decimal points. Hundredths: 8 + 3 = 11, write 1 and regroup 1 tenth. Tenths: 8 + 5 + 1 = 14, write 4 and regroup 1 one. Ones: 0 + 4 + 1 = 5. Answer: 5.41. Check: 5.41 − 4.53 = 0.88.

Line up the decimal points. Write 25.7 as 25.70. Hundredths: 0 − 2 needs a regroup. 1 tenth becomes 10 hundredths: 10 − 2 = 8. Tenths: 6 − 7 needs a regroup. 1 one becomes 10 tenths: 16 − 7 = 9. Ones: 4 − 9 needs a regroup. 1 ten becomes 10 ones: 14 − 9 = 5. Tens: bring down 1. Answer: 15.98. Check: 15.98 + 9.72 = 25.7.

items.q: Add.
items.e: Line up the decimal points. Hundredths: 4 + 9 = 13, write 3 and regroup 1 tenth. Tenths: 7 + 6 + 1 = 14, write 4 and regroup 1 one. Ones: 8 + 2 + 1 = 11, write 1 and regroup 1 ten. Tens: 1 + 4 + 1 = 6. Answer: 61.43. Check: 61.43 − 42.69 = 18.74.

Line up the decimal points. Hundredths: 3 − 6 needs a regroup, but the next place is 0. Regroup 1 one: the ones become 5, each 0 becomes 9, and the hundredths become 13. 13 − 6 = 7. Tenths: 9 − 0 = 9. Ones: 5 − 8 needs a regroup. 1 ten becomes 10 ones: 15 − 8 = 7. Tens: 4 − 3 = 1. Answer: 17.97. Check: 17.97 + 38.06 = 56.03.

items.q: Subtract.
items.e: Line up the decimal points. Write 5 as 5.00. Hundredths: 0 − 5 needs a regroup, but the next place is 0. Regroup 1 one: the ones become 4, each 0 becomes 9, and the hundredths become 10. 10 − 5 = 5. Tenths: 9 − 3 = 6. Ones: 4 − 2 = 2. Answer: 2.65. Check: 2.65 + 2.35 = 5.

items.q: What is 10 − 4.28?
items.e: Line up the decimal points. Write 10 as 10.00. Hundredths: 0 − 8 needs a regroup, but the next place is 0. Regroup 1 ten: the tens become 0, each 0 becomes 9, and the hundredths become 10. 10 − 8 = 2. Tenths: 9 − 2 = 7. Ones: 9 − 4 = 5. Answer: 5.72. Check: 5.72 + 4.28 = 10.

items.q: Subtract.
items.e: Line up the decimal points. Write 3 as 3.0. Tenths: 0 − 6 needs a regroup. 1 one becomes 10 tenths: 10 − 6 = 4. Ones: 2 − 1 = 1. Answer: 1.4. Check: 1.4 + 1.6 = 3.

Line up the decimal points. Hundredths: 5 − 7 needs a regroup, but the next place is 0. Regroup 1 one: the ones become 5, each 0 becomes 9, and the hundredths become 15. 15 − 7 = 8. Tenths: 9 − 3 = 6. Ones: 5 − 2 = 3. Answer: 3.68. Check: 3.68 + 2.37 = 6.05.

items.q: Subtract.
items.e: Line up the decimal points. Write 20 as 20.00. Hundredths: 0 − 5 needs a regroup, but the next place is 0. Regroup 1 ten: the tens become 1, each 0 becomes 9, and the hundredths become 10. 10 − 5 = 5. Tenths: 9 − 4 = 5. Ones: 9 − 7 = 2. Tens: bring down 1. Answer: 12.55. Check: 12.55 + 7.45 = 20.

items.q: Round each number to the nearest whole number. Which is the best estimate for 5.83 + 3.29?
items.e: 5.83 rounds to 6 and 3.29 rounds to 3. 6 + 3 = 9. The exact answer, 9.12, is close to 9.

items.q: Estimate first, then choose the correct answer without working it out exactly: 40 − 18.35
items.e: 40 − 18.35 is about 40 − 18 = 22. Only 21.65 is close to 22. Check by working it out: Write 40 as 40.00. Hundredths: 0 − 5 needs a regroup, but the next place is 0. Regroup 1 ten: the tens become 3, each 0 becomes 9, and the hundredths become 10. 10 − 5 = 5. Tenths: 9 − 3 = 6. Ones: 9 − 8 = 1. Tens: 3 − 1 = 2. Answer: 21.65. Check: 21.65 + 18.35 = 40.

items.q: Estimate first, then choose the correct answer without working it out exactly: 6.07 + 2.9
items.e: 6.07 + 2.9 is about 6 + 3 = 9. Only 8.97 is close to 9. Check by working it out: Write 2.9 as 2.90. Hundredths: 7 + 0 = 7. Tenths: 0 + 9 = 9. Ones: 6 + 2 = 8. Answer: 8.97. Check: 8.97 − 2.9 = 6.07.

items.q: Estimate first, then choose the correct answer without working it out exactly: 13.4 − 5.82
items.e: 13.4 − 5.82 is about 13 − 6 = 7. Only 7.58 is close to 7. Check by working it out: Write 13.4 as 13.40. Hundredths: 0 − 2 needs a regroup. 1 tenth becomes 10 hundredths: 10 − 2 = 8. Tenths: 3 − 8 needs a regroup. 1 one becomes 10 tenths: 13 − 8 = 5. Ones: 2 − 5 needs a regroup. 1 ten becomes 10 ones: 12 − 5 = 7. Answer: 7.58. Check: 7.58 + 5.82 = 13.4.

items.q: Estimate first, then choose the correct answer without working it out exactly: 0.85 + 2.6
items.e: 0.85 + 2.6 is about 1 + 3 = 4. Only 3.45 is close to 4. Check by working it out: Write 2.6 as 2.60. Hundredths: 5 + 0 = 5. Tenths: 8 + 6 = 14, write 4 and regroup 1 one. Ones: 0 + 2 + 1 = 3. Answer: 3.45. Check: 3.45 − 2.6 = 0.85.

items.q: There are no pennies in Canada, so a cash total is rounded to the nearest 5¢. Wei’s total at the corner store is $4.62. He pays with cash. How much does he pay?
items.e: The nearest multiples of 5¢ are $4.60 and $4.65. $4.62 is 2¢ from $4.60 and 3¢ from $4.65, so it rounds down to $4.60. (Totals ending in 1, 2, 6 or 7 cents round down; 3, 4, 8 or 9 round up.)

items.q: At the hockey rink snack bar, Owen buys a hot dog for $3.75 and a hot chocolate for $2.50. How much does he spend?
items.e: Put the two prices together: add. Line up the decimal points. Write 2.5 as 2.50. Hundredths: 5 + 0 = 5. Tenths: 7 + 5 = 12, write 2 and regroup 1 one. Ones: 3 + 2 + 1 = 6. Answer: 6.25. Check: 6.25 − 2.5 = 3.75.

items.q: On a BC Ferries trip to Vancouver Island, Leah buys a muffin for $2.69 and a carton of milk for $1.48. She pays with cash. How much does she pay?
items.e: Step 1, add: $2.69 + $1.48. Hundredths: 9 + 8 = 17, write 7 and regroup 1 tenth. Tenths: 6 + 4 + 1 = 11, write 1 and regroup 1 one. Ones: 2 + 1 + 1 = 4. Total: $4.17. Step 2, cash: $4.17 is 2¢ from $4.15 and 3¢ from $4.20, so she pays $4.15. ($4.17 is what a card would pay.)

items.q: Chloe buys a sandwich for $5.49 and a juice for $2.29. She pays with a debit card. How much is she charged?
items.e: Card and debit payments are charged the exact amount; only cash is rounded to 5¢. $5.49 + $2.29: hundredths 9 + 9 = 18, write 8 and regroup 1 tenth. Tenths 4 + 2 + 1 = 7. Ones 5 + 2 = 7. Answer: $7.78. ($7.80 is the cash price.)

items.q: Ryan pays for a $6.35 lunch with a $10 bill. How much change does he get?
items.e: Change is what is left: subtract. Line up the decimal points. Write 10 as 10.00. Hundredths: 0 − 5 needs a regroup, but the next place is 0. Regroup 1 ten: the tens become 0, each 0 becomes 9, and the hundredths become 10. 10 − 5 = 5. Tenths: 9 − 3 = 6. Ones: 9 − 6 = 3. Answer: 3.65. Check: 3.65 + 6.35 = 10.

items.q: Ji-woo’s groceries come to $13.83. She pays cash with a $20 bill. How much change does she get?
items.e: Step 1, cash total: $13.83 is 2¢ from $13.85 and 3¢ from $13.80, so it rounds to $13.85. Step 2, change: $20.00 − $13.85 = $6.15. Check: $6.15 + $13.85 = $20.00. ($6.17 forgets the cash rounding.)

items.q: It rained in Vancouver on Monday and Tuesday. 12.4 mm of rain fell on Monday and 8.9 mm fell on Tuesday. How much rain fell over the two days?
items.e: Put the two days together: add. Line up the decimal points. Tenths: 4 + 9 = 13, write 3 and regroup 1 one. Ones: 2 + 8 + 1 = 11, write 1 and regroup 1 ten. Tens: 1 + 1 = 2. Answer: 21.3. Check: 21.3 − 8.9 = 12.4.

items.q: On Sports Day, Noah ran the 60 m dash in 11.42 seconds and Mei ran it in 10.87 seconds. How many seconds faster was Mei?
items.e: The faster runner has the smaller time. Find the difference: subtract. Line up the decimal points. Hundredths: 2 − 7 needs a regroup. 1 tenth becomes 10 hundredths: 12 − 7 = 5. Tenths: 3 − 8 needs a regroup. 1 one becomes 10 tenths: 13 − 8 = 5. Ones: 0 − 0 = 0. Tens: 1 − 1 = 0. Answer: 0.55. Check: 0.55 + 10.87 = 11.42.

items.q: At swimming lessons, Nadia swam 25 m in 31.05 seconds. Last month her time was 33.4 seconds. By how many seconds did she improve?
items.e: The improvement is the difference between the two times: subtract. Line up the decimal points. Write 33.4 as 33.40. Hundredths: 0 − 5 needs a regroup. 1 tenth becomes 10 hundredths: 10 − 5 = 5. Tenths: 3 − 0 = 3. Ones: 3 − 1 = 2. Tens: 3 − 3 = 0. Answer: 2.35. Check: 2.35 + 31.05 = 33.4.

items.q: In the long jump, Olivia jumped 2.4 m. Her second jump was 0.35 m longer. How long was the second jump?
items.e: Longer means more: add. Line up the decimal points. Write 2.4 as 2.40. Hundredths: 0 + 5 = 5. Tenths: 4 + 3 = 7. Ones: 2 + 0 = 2. Answer: 2.75. Check: 2.75 − 0.35 = 2.4.

items.q: A coho salmon in the Fraser River is 0.64 m long. A chinook salmon is 0.92 m long. How much longer is the chinook salmon?
items.e: How much longer means find the difference: subtract. Line up the decimal points. Hundredths: 2 − 4 needs a regroup. 1 tenth becomes 10 hundredths: 12 − 4 = 8. Tenths: 8 − 6 = 2. Answer: 0.28. Check: 0.28 + 0.64 = 0.92.

items.q: A water bottle holds 1 L. Arjun drinks 0.45 L on a hike at Grouse Mountain. How much water is left?
items.e: Take away what he drank: subtract. Line up the decimal points. Write 1 as 1.00. Hundredths: 0 − 5 needs a regroup, but the next place is 0. Regroup 1 one: the ones become 0, each 0 becomes 9, and the hundredths become 10. 10 − 5 = 5. Tenths: 9 − 4 = 5. Answer: 0.55. Check: 0.55 + 0.45 = 1.

items.q: A roll of ribbon is 3 m long. The class cuts off 1.25 m for a banner. How much ribbon is left?
items.e: Take the part cut off away: subtract. Line up the decimal points. Write 3 as 3.00. Hundredths: 0 − 5 needs a regroup, but the next place is 0. Regroup 1 one: the ones become 2, each 0 becomes 9, and the hundredths become 10. 10 − 5 = 5. Tenths: 9 − 2 = 7. Ones: 2 − 1 = 1. Answer: 1.75. Check: 1.75 + 1.25 = 3.

items.q: Jasleen’s family walks 3.6 km on the Stanley Park seawall before lunch and 2.85 km after lunch. How far do they walk altogether?
items.e: Altogether means add. Line up the decimal points. Write 3.6 as 3.60. Hundredths: 0 + 5 = 5. Tenths: 6 + 8 = 14, write 4 and regroup 1 one. Ones: 3 + 2 + 1 = 6. Answer: 6.45. Check: 6.45 − 2.85 = 3.6.

items.q: The Terry Fox Run at Ava’s school is 2.5 km long. She has run 1.75 km so far. How much farther does she have to run?
items.e: How much farther means find what is left: subtract. Line up the decimal points. Write 2.5 as 2.50. Hundredths: 0 − 5 needs a regroup. 1 tenth becomes 10 hundredths: 10 − 5 = 5. Tenths: 4 − 7 needs a regroup. 1 one becomes 10 tenths: 14 − 7 = 7. Ones: 1 − 1 = 0. Answer: 0.75. Check: 0.75 + 1.75 = 2.5.

items.q: Lucas pays by card for a book at $12.99 and a pencil case at $4.49. What is the total?
items.e: Total means add. A card pays the exact amount. Line up the decimal points. Hundredths: 9 + 9 = 18, write 8 and regroup 1 tenth. Tenths: 9 + 4 + 1 = 14, write 4 and regroup 1 one. Ones: 2 + 4 + 1 = 7. Tens: bring down 1. Answer: 17.48. Check: 17.48 − 4.49 = 12.99.

items.q: Emma’s backpack has a mass of 3.2 kg. She takes out a lunch bag with a mass of 0.65 kg. What is the mass of the backpack now?
items.e: Take away what was taken out: subtract. Line up the decimal points. Write 3.2 as 3.20. Hundredths: 0 − 5 needs a regroup. 1 tenth becomes 10 hundredths: 10 − 5 = 5. Tenths: 1 − 6 needs a regroup. 1 one becomes 10 tenths: 11 − 6 = 5. Ones: bring down 2. Answer: 2.55. Check: 2.55 + 0.65 = 3.2.

items.q: Mateo has $20 at the school spring fair. He buys a plant for $8.45 and a pie for $6.75. How much money does he have left?
Kai measures the new snow at school in Prince George on three days: 12.4 cm, 9.8 cm and 4.6 cm. What is the total snowfall?
items.e: Total means add all three days. Line up the decimal points. Tenths: 4 + 8 + 6 = 18, write 8 and regroup 1 one. Ones: 2 + 9 + 4 + 1 = 16, write 6 and regroup 1 ten. Tens: 1 + 1 = 2. Answer: 26.8.

items.q: What number goes in the box? ☐ + 2.45 = 6
items.e: Use subtraction: 6 − 2.45 = 6.00 − 2.45 = 3.55. Check: 3.55 + 2.45 = 6.00 = 6. (4.45 forgets to write the zeros: 6 − 2 = 4, then brings down .45. 8.45 adds instead of subtracting.)
